subject: Control plane implementation plan: SIEM-ready audit export (beta)
body:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 20, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Control plane implementation plan: SIEM-ready audit export (beta)
Attachments: SIEM_Audit_Export_Control_Plane_Plan_v0.9.pdf, Audit_Export_RACI_and_Timeline_v3.xlsx

All — sharing a concrete plan for the Control Plane pieces needed for the SIEM-ready audit export beta, with owners + dates. This is intended to unblock the exporter team and keep us inside the beta window Naomi outlined.

Summary (Control Plane scope for beta)
1) Export Config CRUD API (destinations + credentials refs + filters + backfill window)
2) RBAC permissions/scopes for export management (least privilege + audit trail)
3) Export Status endpoint for Console (lag, last success, last error, per-destination health)
4) Rollout controls (tenant allowlist + kill switch; admin tooling)

Dependencies we need to hold steady
- Audit Event Schema v2: stable event_id + category taxonomy (required for dedup + filters)
- PII redaction policy signoff on schema fields and “what is/isn’t in audit logs”

Proposed milestone dates (beta cohort: hosted + dedicated)
- Mar 24: API shapes frozen (request/response + validation rules) + FF strategy finalized
- Mar 28: Export Config CRUD endpoints merged behind feature flag, staged in dev
- Apr 4: RBAC permissions merged + default roles mapped (admin vs auditor)
- Apr 11: Status endpoint merged + Console integration unblocked
- Apr 18: Tenant allowlist + kill switch wired end-to-end; start internal alpha

Owners (for planning; not all are cc’d here)
- Config CRUD API + storage/migrations: Ethan Park’s org (Benji O., Michael N.)
- RBAC: Kaitlyn N.
- Filtering validation rules (API-side): Jordan L. (policy engine)
- Status endpoint + caching/tenancy checks: Chloe M.
- Feature flags/allowlist admin: Connor O.

Open questions / asks
1) Marcus/Olga: can we treat “export config changes” as audit events in v2 as part of beta (create/update/delete/rotate creds)? It’s part of a compliance story and is small, but needs approval.
2) Neha: can you sanity-check the SLO signals we expose in the status endpoint for on-call usefulness (lag/last_success/last_error + adapter error counts)?
3) Naomi: confirm the beta cohort target start date you’re holding customers to. I assumed “internal alpha by 4/18” and “beta accounts by early May,” but want to align.

Notes
- We are explicitly not doing Private/on-prem controls in this beta (document follow-on), but we should avoid hard-coding cloud-only assumptions into the API.
- Secrets handling: Control Plane should only store references (vault/KMS handle). No raw tokens/keys in config payloads beyond initial creation.

If no objections by EOD Friday, I’ll socialize this plan in the Platform staff sync and we’ll staff accordingly.

— Priya

Priya Natarajan
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 20, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Control plane implementation plan: SIEM-ready audit export (beta)

This looks right to me.

Beta timing: I told customers “May” with explicit caveats (limited backfill window, hosted/dedicated only, at-least-once w/ downstream dedup). Internally I’d like to target:
- week of May 5: first 1–2 tenants (Splunk + S3)
- week of May 12: add Datadog tenant

Re #1: +1 that config changes should generate audit events. If we can’t get it into v2 emissions in time, we can still log internally but it’s a gap for compliance narratives.

Also: can we add “test destination” endpoint to the plan, even if basic? It’s a big UX ask from design/CS.

Naomi



From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 20, 2025 at 11:14 AM PT
Subject: Re: Control plane implementation plan: SIEM-ready audit export (beta)

Thanks Priya.

On config change audit events: yes, but with two constraints we should lock early:
1) No secrets in the audit payload (even “last 4 chars” style) — just secret_ref ids and destination type.
2) For destination “hostnames/URLs”, we should log the normalized host (and maybe port) rather than full URL/query to avoid accidental token leakage.

If we add a “test destination” endpoint, it should be careful not to become an SSRF vector. At minimum:
- validate destination hostname against allowlist rules
- no arbitrary headers beyond the expected auth mechanism
- structured logging must redact

If your team can share the draft endpoint contract, I’ll get Security Eng eyes on it quickly.

— Marcus



From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 20, 2025 at 1:27 PM PT
Subject: Re: Control plane implementation plan: SIEM-ready audit export (beta)

Plan is workable.

Re: status endpoint signals — +1 to exposing a small, stable set:
- export_lag_seconds (p50/p95 if you can, but single value is OK for beta)
- last_success_at (timestamp)
- last_error_at + last_error_code (enum-ish) + last_error_message (truncated, no PII)
- is_paused (manual or auto-paused)

One ask: can the status endpoint include “checkpoint age” (how old is the last persisted checkpoint)? That helps on-call differentiate downstream throttling vs exporter stuck.

Also flagging: if the plan is internal alpha by 4/18, we need alert rules + dashboards in place by then, or we’ll be flying blind. Even a barebones dashboard is fine.

Neha



From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 20, 2025 at 2:09 PM PT
Subject: Re: Control plane implementation plan: SIEM-ready audit export (beta)

Adding the compliance lens:

- Strong preference that we do emit audit events for export configuration lifecycle (create/update/delete/enable/disable/rotate). That’s often explicitly asked in SOC2/ISO questionnaires.
- We should document retention vs export responsibilities in the admin docs + FAQ, but for the control plane: please ensure backfill window semantics are unambiguous (e.g., “up to N days” and “best-effort within at-least-once”).

If you can share the “Evidence language” you intend to use for the beta (esp. around delivery guarantees and what “at-least-once” implies), I’ll align with GRC.

Olga



From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Mar 21, 2025 at 4:38 PM PT
Subject: Re: Control plane implementation plan: SIEM-ready audit export (beta)

All — super helpful, thank you.

Updates I’m making to the plan (v1.0):

1) Add “Test destination” endpoint (scoped)
- Goal: validate credentials + basic connectivity + write permission (for S3) / HEC accept (for Splunk) / intake accept (Datadog)
- Security constraints per Marcus: strict destination validation + egress allowlist, no arbitrary headers, redact logs, store only secret_ref
- Target: behind FF, available for internal alpha only by Apr 11; customer-facing UI can follow.

2) Status endpoint fields (for beta)
- export_lag_seconds
- checkpoint_age_seconds (good call)
- last_success_at
- last_error_at
- last_error_code (normalized)
- is_paused + pause_reason

3) Audit events for export-config lifecycle
- We’ll treat these as first-class audit events in schema v2; no secrets; normalized destination host.
- I’m going to ask Marcus to nominate a Security reviewer for the specific event payloads when we open the PRs.

4) Beta dates
- Aligning to Naomi’s schedule: first tenants week of May 5. That means we need internal alpha stable by ~Apr 18 and “known gaps” documented by Apr 25.

Next actions
- I’ll send a 1-pager API contract (CRUD + test + status) Monday AM for quick review.
- Naomi: I’ll mirror your customer-facing caveats in the plan so we don’t drift.
- Olga: I’ll draft evidence language for “at-least-once export” and backfill semantics and route for your review.

Have a good weekend.

— Priya

Priya Natarajan
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
